messages:
jamie: Heads up — seeing ~6 GPU nodes in asia-east1-a (nodepool= gpu-preemptible-ops) flip to NotReady / NoSchedule over the last 10m. A bunch of GPU pods are now Pending. Autoscaler already removed two other nodes. Anyone seeing driver/device-plugin errors? :eyes:

sre-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scaled down 2 nodes from gpu-preemptible-ops at 2026-03-18T02:12:34Z (reason: low utilization)

alex: grabbing logs from one of the affected nodes. dmesg shows repeated failures trying to register nvidia modules: ```Mar 18 02:05:21 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and required key missing
Mar 18 02:05:21 kernel: nvidia: failed to load nvidia_modeset: -22
Mar 18 02:05:21 kubelet[1234]: error registering device plugin: timeout waiting for device-plugin registration
```

priya: Are these preemptible instances? startup order race between driver install and containerd/kubelet can leave device-plugin unable to register. Which image and driver installer are we using?

jamie: Yes preemptible. Image is custom gke-gpu-ubuntu-2024-09 with startup-script that apt-installs the driver and then kicks off the nvidia-device-plugin DaemonSet.

alex: kubectl describe node gpu-node-asia-3 shows: Conditions: Ready Unknown (KubeletNotReady: driver ops failed). Events: "Device plugin registration timeout" and "Node status changed to NoSchedule". The plugin containers are CrashLoopBackOff: logs: "failed to open /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory"

maria: cluster-autoscaler note: CA avoids removing nodes with running pods, but if the pods are stuck Pending the algorithm can consider low utilization and scale down other nodes — net result: we end up with fewer healthy nodes and more pending GPU pods. That's dangerous for preemptible pools.

ken: Short-term mitigation: 1) cordon remaining gpu nodes so CA won't scale them down: `kubectl cordon <node>` 2) roll the nvidia-driver DaemonSet with a retry init container to modprobe on host and wait for /dev/nvidia* before starting plugin 3) add annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"` to the nodepool deployment to stop CA from touching it until we stabilize.

jamie: I cordoned the 3 surviving nodes and bumped the driver DaemonSet image to v1.2.3 which includes exponential retries for modprobe. Restarting pod on each node now.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: rolled DaemonSet "nvidia-driver-installer" -> image v1.2.3, 3/3 updated, 3/3 ready.

alex: After the restart, 4 nodes came back to Ready within ~90s. Device plugin logs show successful registration: `Registered device plugin for NVIDIA GPUs` and `/dev/nvidia0` present.

priya: Follow-up items: - Bake the working driver into the node image (avoid startup-script race) - Move critical workloads to a non-preemptible pool or mark them with podTopologySpread/priority so CA won't evict their nodes - Add healthcheck to cluster-autoscaler to detect excessive recent scale-down events for GPU pools

maria: Also file INFRA ticket to reconcile cost vs reliability: switching the small critical pool to on-demand GPUs will add roughly ~$0.6/hr per GPU but prevents this class of failure and reduces churn.

jamie: Created INFRA-342, assigned to eng-infra. For now leaving gpu-preemptible-ops cordoned and added the CA annotation. Will monitor. Thanks all :thumbsup:
